paragraphs: Once there was a frog who lived at the bottom of a well. He had been born there, grown up there, and never once climbed out. Swamiji added with a smile that the frog surely had eyes, whatever the scientists might say, and that it spent its days busily clearing the water of every worm and germ. All that hard work paid off: the frog grew sleek and plump and very comfortable in his little world.
One day a stranger dropped in, quite literally. A frog from the sea fell into the well.
"Where have you come from?" asked the well frog.

"The sea? How big is that? Is it as big as my well?" And to show what he meant, the well frog jumped from one side of the well to the other. The sea frog laughed and told him that comparing the sea to a little well made no sense. The well frog tried a bigger jump. "Is it this big, then?" The sea frog shook his head: the question itself was nonsense.

At last the well frog lost patience. Nothing, he declared, could possibly be larger than his well. This newcomer must be a liar, and the best thing was to throw him out. Swamiji told this story to explain why people quarrel over religion and ideas: each of us sits in a small well and imagines it is the whole world.
learn: Our opinions are often shaped by the small space we grew up in: one city, one community, one feed. When someone describes a world bigger than ours, the honest response is curiosity, not calling them a liar. Step out of your well before you judge the sea.
